body_html:
How to think about it

A pulse is a single disturbance; a wave is a series of pulses. In a transverse wave the particles move at right angles to the direction of the wave; in a longitudinal wave they move parallel to it. Waves carry energy, not matter.

The amplitude is the maximum displacement from rest; the wavelength λ is the distance between two crests. The frequency f is the number of waves per second, and the period T = 1/f. When two pulses meet, their displacements add (superposition): crest + crest gives constructive interference, crest + trough gives destructive interference.

Example

f = 5 Hz, λ = 2 m. Wave speed?

v = fλ

Answer: 10 m·s⁻¹

Example

A wave has a period of 0.2 s. Frequency?

f = 1/T

Answer: 5 Hz

Common mistakes

  • Measuring the amplitude from crest to trough.
  • Thinking the medium moves along with the wave.
  • Mixing up period and frequency.

faq.q: What happens when two pulses of the same size meet crest to trough?
faq.a: They cancel each other out for a moment (destructive interference), then carry on unchanged.
